findings.text: The guard resolves the review role without the arguments the dispatch resolves it with: `routing.resolve_role(config, "review")` leaves spec_level at its empty default, while the dispatch resolves the same role at spec_level="exact" (reckon/crew/recovery_review_dispatch.py:2949, reckon/crew/plan_review.py:5794). A `roles.review.by_spec_level.exact` overlay carrying a `launch` (or a backend with a different `launch`) is therefore skipped here and the guard judges a launch the dispatch never asks for. The live ~/.config/reckon/flight.yaml sets only `effort` under review.by_spec_level, so no divergence occurs today, but the commit's own claim that one resolver decides the launch for both is true of the helper and not of its arguments.

The section's done_when requires the test files importing the modified modules to add no failure against the base revision, but the recorded importer arms (logs/importer-base.log and logs/importer-head.log) were measured at f0506fe0162a, one commit before the reviewed head, and the reviewed head changes this production module. The head arm (logs/after-arm.log) covers only tests/test_a_refused_plan_review_writes_nothing.py and tests/test_staged_write_inventory.py, so the importer clause is not measured at the revision this review reads.
